prompt: What is the product of the solutions to $x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0$?
hint: You can find both solutions and multiply them. There is also a rule that gives the product straight from two of the coefficients.

hints.text: You can find both solutions and multiply them. There is also a rule that gives the product straight from two of the coefficients.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a factorable one: $x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0$ has roots $2$ and $3$, whose product is $6$ — exactly the constant term. That is the $c/a$ rule in miniature.
The solutions of $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ multiply to $\dfrac{c}{a}$. In this equation $a = 1$ and $c = -12$, so divide them.
The product is $\dfrac{-12}{1} = -12$, so the solutions multiply to $-12$.

learningObjective: Use the product-of-roots relationship for a quadratic.
explanation: For any quadratic $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$, the product of the solutions is $\dfrac{c}{a}$, which here is $\dfrac{-12}{1} = -12$.
Factoring confirms the rule: $(x - 6)(x + 2) = 0$ has solutions $6$ and $-2$.
Multiplying them gives $6 \times (-2) = -12$, so the product of the solutions is $-12$.

alternativeExplanations.title: A negative product is information
steps: If the product of the roots is negative, the two roots must have opposite signs.
If the product is positive, they share a sign — and then the sum tells you which.
Reading the signs off $b$ and $c$ before factoring often tells you what pair to look for.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The sum, 4, is offered right beside the product; so is +12, the product with a dropped sign.
Product is c/a WITH ITS SIGN: −12/1. Check against the factored roots 6 and −2: their product is −12 ✓
